title: That Familiar Bitterness
subtitle: Welcome to the other side of life.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: We're all quite used to the "language disorder" by now, so that isn't much of a problem, and there isn't much need for him to communicate with anyone.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: But what does concern me is that moving tower. A brand new variable ...

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: What was it again? There was an expression I heard when I was trying to research Kiperina's and Name Day's arcane skills.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Oh! That's the one! "People can only borrow language; they cannot reach the reality behind it."

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: We need to start considering the possibility of evacuating Adler early.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: I doubt he'll agree.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Then prepare to evacuate him by force. If necessary.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: From what we've seen so far, the situation is far worse than predicted. Not only has the "language disorder" encompassed the whole toybox, but it's starting to leak out of it, too.
Ulrich gestures to Hissabeth. The silver patterns on his uniform are slowly fading. She examines him carefully and reaches a quick conclusion.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Oh, you're right. You HAVE been standing closest to the box.
She exchanges a look with Ulrich and picks up the communicator.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Alright, I'll tell him. Saves the two of you from bickering again.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Adler, can you hear me?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I hope you have some good news.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Sorry for what I'm about to say, but I'll keep it straight: the toybox's instability is higher than predicted. We advise you to return early.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: If you can't retrieve the core soon, we'll have to use our backup plan—blowing up the box.
Enigma goes quiet for a few seconds.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: And Bottlebrain agrees with this?

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: I didn't want this either. But right now, there's no better solution.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Ulrich, what are you saying?

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: The disorder is spreading to Laplace again. Your time in the box is limited.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: And according to the LSCC Safety Management Regulations, ensuring your safety is the higher priority.
Enigma takes a deep breath, yet doesn't argue.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I understand. Give me two hours. If I don't make any progress, I'll return.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Then we can blow it up together.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Two hours, Adler. We'll do whatever we can to help.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Researchers X, Medicine Pocket, and Hissabeth are currently dealing with the spread of the disorder. I also need to step away for a moment to deal with it.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Researcher Pointer is monitoring the toybox's situation. If you run into any danger, be sure to request assistance immediately.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I will.
He looks up again at the white spire—seemingly within reach, yet forever beyond it.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Hmm?
Maybe it's just his imagination, but for a moment, it felt like he was closer to it.
The journey that follows is too quiet, almost dull. The only thing Enigma can do is note the changes in the surrounding scenery.
He keeps his eyes peeled, but no other familiar faces appear.
Until a heated argument, even for Laplace's standards, breaks out ahead.
A researcher and an administrator argue on opposite sides of a desk in a strange, yet somehow familiar, scene.

items.speaker: Research Staff
items.text: I am NOT redoing the material reimbursement.

items.speaker: Administrative Staff
items.text: Then you can choose not to submit it. But I must remind you that the reimbursement deadline is this Friday.
Enigma feels a familiar irritation itch at him as the argument dredges up his own unpleasant memories.

items.speaker: Research Staff
items.text: Picrasma extract has extremely potent side effects.

items.speaker: Administrative Staff
items.text: Laplace ought to tear down the building and install turf!

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Hmm?
The researcher suddenly draws a gun on his colleague. Perhaps he doesn't think of him as one.

items.speaker: Research Staff
items.text: Are-are-are-are you done??!! @# You're wasting Laplace resources!
Bang. The staff member drops to the ground. Enigma isn't sure whether he should step forward and do something.

items.speaker: Research Staff
items.text: Liberation for all the Critters in the canteen!
Before he can decide, a pack of Critters pours out from behind the researcher piece and lunges at him.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: What on ...?!
Stopping them isn't difficult. After so many explorations, Enigma has grown used to it.
The communicator's ring interrupts his mulling over the sudden change.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: We're back. This time the disorder's symptoms are visual. Nothing too serious.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: It's a shame you can't see us right now—gathered around the toybox with symbols floating around our heads.
Enigma pictures it and can't help but rub his temples.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: What's the situation?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Nothing much to report. Though, a piece just did something I'm sure we've all wanted to.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: He applied for a massive amount of funds?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: No, he killed the administrator who asked him to resubmit his invoice, then led a dozen Critters in an attempted uprising.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Very extreme. Interesting.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Now, now, there's no one here who wants to do anything like that to our colleagues.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: To each their own. I'd like to confirm something.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: You just returned this moment, yes? Was anybody thinking about invoices, the canteen, or anything related to Picrasma candy just now?

items.speaker: X
items.text: Hey, why all the questions? Mr. Enigma, this isn't exactly the time for a workplace interview.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Come on! Stop the chatter and tell me, quickly!

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Oh, you mean you think our observations out here are having an impact in there?

items.speaker: Medicine Pocket
items.text: Right! The approval you owe me, it's still in the back of my mind! You already got it, right? The bottle of Picrasma—

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: That's the one.
His hypothesis is confirmed.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Now, I need you to give me some time.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Stay away from the box. Do not observe my movements.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: I see. We'll avoid any eye contact with the toybox.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Remember, we have forced evacuation measures in place, Adler.
Silence follows.
Enigma holds his breath and watches.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: As expected.
The Critters slowly disappear, and the blood-covered researcher shuffles back to the desk—now simply some grids.

items.speaker: Research Staff
items.text: Hey, pal. Coming through!

items.speaker: Research Staff
items.text: Sorry, need to reorganize all these receipts ASAP. You heard him, didn't you? The deadline's Friday! Don't your projects need reimbursements, too?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Thanks for the reminder, but my team is still waiting for funding approval.

items.speaker: Research Staff
items.text: Ah. Must be tough. Hang in there!
He pats Enigma on the shoulder, then limps toward the far wall where there should be a lab.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Ulrich, I assume you've also come to the same conclusion.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: The correlation between the degree of observation and the toybox's abnormalities.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Exactly. Put this down in your report: The reason I made you all leave wasn't because I harbored any ill will toward my colleagues.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: As we all know, every new observer adds a degree of freedom. The higher the degree of freedom, the harder it is to converge at a single point.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Someone wants to see a dark room, so they turn on a flashlight.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: But if ten people in different corners of the room simultaneously turn on their flashlights, between all the beams of light, not one of them can see clearly.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: This we understood. But what we failed to account for was the light shining through the window—the people outside the room.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Not only do those who enter the toybox increase interference, but so too do those who observe from the outside!
The communicator goes silent. Clearly, Ulrich is thinking fast.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: An astonishing conclusion, Adler, but it's a line of thought worth testing.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Do you think two hours of basic cryptography training would be enough for one of our colleagues to enter the box and take your place?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: No need to complicate things.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: We can cut off communications now.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: What did you say?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Turn off the flashlight, and the room will return to its original appearance.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Every flashlight, including my own.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Let me remind you again: you're not an arcanist. You can't detect the arcane fluctuations in the toybox on your own.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Yes I can. Although the effects won't last for long.
He pops open the metal tube in his pocket.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I still have faith in science, even in an era where rain falls in reverse. It's reliable by nature: systematic, comprehensive, replicable.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: As for arcanum, I may as well make the most of it while it's mine to use. Thankfully, its basic applications don't require deep understanding.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I'll ensure my own safety.
A rare silence follows from the other end of the communicator. As the candies drop into Enigma's palm, the reply finally comes.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Of course. You're an exceptional researcher and our greatest cryptographer.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: You still have thirty minutes, plus the two additional hours we've approved.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Best of luck. See you soon, Adler.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: See you soon, Ulrich.
He nods and hangs up.
He's on his own now. Enigma draws a deep breath and closes his eyes.
Not to observe, but to sense.
An unfinished antidote and a trace of test poison—to keep Manus Vindictae from using it to cause another tragedy.
He's tried it countless times. It should work.
The taste of Picrasma extract creeps up from the back of his tongue. Enigma's one-quarter arcanist blood briefly awakens.
Emotion and reason.
Arcanist and human.
Arcanum and science.
Science carried him to the point where there seemed to be no going forward.
Arcanum has allowed him to touch the faint glimmer of light in the cracks.
In the deepest dark, there's a soft knock on a brick.
